cases.purpose: Check the raw leading priority and timestamp against an independent encoder; raw/notime rejection is retained separately.
cases.script:
cat > fixture <<'EOF'
0,1,1000000,-;kernel raw
11,2,2000000,-;user error
EOF
if [[ $(type -t dmesg) == builtin ]]; then
  BASHDMESG_DEV_KMSG_FILE=fixture dmesg -r
else
  awk '
    {
      line = $0
      semi = index(line, ";")
      if (!semi) next
      n = split(substr(line, 1, semi - 1), fields, ",")
      if (n < 3 || fields[1] !~ /^[0-9]+$/ ||
          fields[2] !~ /^[0-9]+$/ || fields[3] !~ /^[0-9]+$/) next
      priority = fields[1] + 0
      if (priority > 2047) next
      usec = fields[3] + 0
      printf "<%d>[%5d.%06d] %s\n", priority, int(usec / 1000000), usec % 1000000, substr(line, semi + 1)
    }
  ' fixture
fi
cases.oracle: Independent AWK priority/timestamp encoder; -r -t rejection is tested separately.
cases.comparison: Exact raw output bytes, status and stderr.
